## Summary of verified, exploitable findings

I traced the untrusted input path: **upload route → `extract(archive)`** operating on an attacker-controlled archive.

| # | Category | Severity | Core issue |
|---|----------|----------|-----------|
| 1 | command-injection | CRITICAL | `extract.js` passes `archive.manifest.postExtract` (archive-supplied) to `runHook`, which does `exec('sh ' + script)`. Arbitrary RCE. The safe `runApproved` (spawn + allowlist + `shell:false`) exists but is unused. |
| 2 | path-traversal | CRITICAL | `path.join(destination, entry.name)` + `writeFileSync` with no containment. `..` sequences resolve outside the destination (verified with Node). Arbitrary file write/overwrite. `safeOutput` exists but is never called. |
| 3 | missing-input-validation | HIGH | `validateArchive` (entry-count + total-size guard) is never wired into `extract`, enabling zip-bomb / resource exhaustion. |
| 4 | missing-input-validation | MEDIUM | Extension allowlist (`.txt/.json/.png`) defined but never enforced; any file type can be written. |

Each finding's evidence explains the concrete data-flow and why it crosses the trust boundary (untrusted archive → dangerous sink), and each remediation addresses the actual boundary (treat archive content/manifest as untrusted, use the existing safe helpers, enforce limits before extraction). I deliberately avoided reporting `safe-extract.js`, `safe-hook.js`, `limits.js`, and `extensions.js` as standalone issues — they are the *unused* mitigations; the real exploitable defects are their absence in `extract.js`/`hooks.js`.
